H7: Jealousy Can Capture Monogamy or Free Love
e1-P1: Any community that lasts will eventually reorganize itself due to attraction and pair-bonding. When two exes live in the same city, they can move to different sides of the city. When they're part of a thirty-person commune, they may still be in the same kitchen the next morning, working in the same team, attending the same meetings, sharing childcare and the same friends. A couple's jealousy or breakup becomes a problem for the entire community, because it will change the loyalties, the sleeping arrangements, the work load, the kids, the alliances, and sometimes who's leaving.
e1-P2: The discussion generally goes straight to "should people be monogamous or free-love?" but as I discuss in my Romance Guide, this is one level too late in the conversation. The community problem is that, in close quarters, jealousy gets magnified, and it can capture either system.
e1-P3: Rigid monogamy can turn fear and possession into a moral law. With free love, if there's no inner pl/ork, the same fear can just get spread over a bigger spreadsheet. And whatever label you put on a relationship, it won't release childhood panic. It won't release comparison or abandonment terror either, or the wish to control another person.
e1-P4: I don't think it should be up to the community to decide for everyone what form relationships will take. People can make different agreements with each other, in pairs, threes, fours, whatever. They can change those agreements as they wish. And they can ask for support when those agreements bring up old material.
e1-P5: Whatever forms people choose, I do think that housing, security for kids, membership and access to common necessities should not be contingent on a person staying in some agreement with a person they're romantically involved with.
e1-P6: ZEGG and Tamera have spent decades experimenting with relationships inside community. Their answers are not a set of commandments that everyone must follow. But they are an example of how a community can acknowledge the erotic aspects of life. It's not necessary for twenty adults to pretend they've become neutral colleagues just because the bylaws say so.
e1-P7: Jealousy can't become the hidden governor. That's the non-negotiable part, for me. It has to be able to come to the surface and be talked about. It has to be felt in the body. People need to be able to explore it without being humiliated, and let it go gradually, rather than converting it into punishment or policy.
e1-P8: The group can help support people and enforce basic boundaries without determining what kind of relationships people have. People will still disagree, though. It's more realistic to assume that than to declare the matter solved.
